title: Derived tensor with a scalar-restricted sheaf on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\varphi:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor and extension of scalars [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], termwise restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and derived tensor as obtained by the K-flat localization [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For every $H\in D(\mathcal R)$ and every sheaf $N$ of $\mathcal S$-modules placed in degree zero, there is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal R)$, natural in both $H$ and $N$,
$$H\otimes_{\mathcal R}^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\bigl((H\otimes_{\mathcal R}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal S}^{\mathbf L}N\bigr).$$
Here the inner extension is valued in $D(\mathcal S)$ as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For any K-flat flat-term representative $P\to H$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the displayed isomorphism is represented by the balanced chain isomorphism
$$P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_\varphi((P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal S}N),\qquad x\otimes n\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes n,$$
whose inverse sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes n$ to $x\otimes sn$. These representatives compute both derived objects and give the same natural isomorphism independently of the chosen representative. No flatness of $\mathcal S$ over $\mathcal R$, boundedness of $H$, or finite Tor amplitude of $N$ is assumed.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact and commutes with small direct sums. Indeed, by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] it changes only the scalar action, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] kernels and cokernels have the same underlying abelian sheaves before and after restriction; the same holds for direct sums. The forgetful functor is faithful, so an underlying zero cohomology sheaf is zero as a module sheaf. Thus termwise restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(\mathcal S)\to D(\mathcal R)$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), applied to both coefficient sheaves

proof.text: Choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $P\to C$ of a complex representing $H$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P_S=P\otimes_R S$ is K-flat with flat $S$-terms, without flatness of $S/R$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $Q_SP_S$ canonically represents $H\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$, compatibly with maps of resolutions.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), identity topos and coefficient map

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-site-balanced-tensor-chain] to $P,N$. Its sheaf chain isomorphism $a_{P,N}$ has exactly the two generator formulas required here and is natural in both variables, including homotopies in $P$. By [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization], applied over $R$ to $(P,UN[0])$ and over $S$ to $(P_S,N[0])$, these two total complexes compute the two desired derived tensors with their specified canonical comparisons. Apply the exact restriction from step 1 to the second comparison. Conjugating $Q_R(a_{P,N})$ by these comparisons and the scalar-extension comparison of step 2 gives the required isomorphism on K-flat flat-term representatives.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor) and preceding construction; comparison of one-sided and two-sided K-flat computation

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_R$ be the homotopy subcategory of K-flat flat-term complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $Q_R|_{\mathcal P_R}$ is a localization at its quasi-isomorphisms. The isomorphisms in step 3 and their inverses are natural transformations with values in $\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Mod}(S),D(R))$: naturality in $P$ uses the two new lemmas and the scalar-extension comparison, and naturality in $N$ uses their other variables. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] extends both transformations uniquely along this localization. Their composites extend the identities, so they remain inverse, simultaneously natural in $H,N$. For any specified resolution $p:P\to C$, naturality along $Q_Rp$ identifies the component with $a_{P,N}$ under the comparisons in steps 2-3. Uniqueness gives the same component for every other resolution, without requiring a chain map between the resolutions. All complexes and coefficient maps were arbitrary; no boundedness, Tor-amplitude, or coefficient-flatness hypothesis entered.

The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to base. The proof is now 4 assembly steps (2670 characters, at most 3000). The item is not in the dropped list and no other group has superseded it. Base steps 1 and 4 are kept verbatim as steps 1 and 2, and base step 7 is kept in full as step 4. Base steps 2-3 became lem-trf-site-balanced-tensor-chain (1623 characters): both generator formulas, sheaf maps including the S-action through N, the d_P⊗1 chain structure, and naturality including homotopies. Base steps 5-6 became lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization (1954 characters): preservation of quasi-isomorphisms in both orders, and a unique c_{T,M} normalized by c_{T,V}=δ_{T,V}^{-1} and natural in both T and M. Nothing was shortened or dropped, and neither node restates the item. Both new statements are true. I checked the balancing relations, the inverse identities and the Koszul sign, and the localization existence/uniqueness through lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent and the localization universal property. Small cases P=R[0], T=B[0], S=0, φ=id, Z→F_p and Z/4→F_2 all hold. I verified the assembly orientation c_R, then Q(a), then Res c_S^{-1}, and the hypotheses: P_S is K-flat with flat terms by lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings, and M is arbitrary. Sources are Stacks 03EK (sites-modules l.3551) and 06YP/06YT/06YU (sites-cohomology l.3011-3310), plus blueprint main-20261015 lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth Step 2 (l.64-68). No SGA is cited. I accept the six generic tool_uses.
